patch.value: GH-887: terminal create contract is non-atomic and inconsistent across importer-facing closure metadata

GitHub issue #887 reports that importers upgrading to 2026.8.3 repeatedly implemented create-then-parse-id-then-close workflows for source records already terminal. Although create can currently satisfy close-reason governance through --resolution, the contract does not present a coherent create-time closure surface for close reason, completion time, expected/actual evidence, and source provenance, and the multi-command fallback is non-atomic and slow.

A single SDK primitive is authoritative for atomic create-plus-terminal-transition semantics and governance validation; CLI, MCP, contracts, completion, docs, and external package examples expose coherent close reason, completion time, resolution, expected, actual, and source provenance inputs; The mutation receipt is stable and typed; imported terminal records cannot silently degrade to open on parser mismatch or partial failure; Batch and isolated npm/Bun package consumers prove performance and behavior across GitHub, CSV, and Beads importer patterns
pm-cli 2026.8.3 with GitHub, CSV, and Beads external importers
Import an already-closed source record while require_close_reason is enabled; compare create flags with close flags and implement the documented fallback across hundreds of records
One typed SDK/CLI mutation atomically creates terminal source records with complete author-supplied closure provenance and stable receipt semantics
Importers couple to a partial create contract or perform multiple subprocess calls with a crash window and duplicated parsing logic
Bulk migrations are slower, non-atomic, and can silently leave terminal source work open
